title: Inverse design of porous materials: a diffusion model approach

metadata.authors: Park J, Gill APS, Moosavi SM, Kim J

source_summary: A newly developed diffusion model for generating pure silica zeolite demonstrates superior performance over GANs in creating novel crystalline porous materials and excels in inverse design tasks, highlighting the transformative potential of diffusion models in material discovery.
abstract: The success of diffusion models in the field of image processing has propelled the creation of software such as Dall-E, Midjourney and Stable Diffusion, which are tools used for text-to-image generation. Mapping this workflow onto material discovery, a new diffusion model was developed for the generation of pure silica zeolite, marking one of the first applications of diffusion models to porous materials. Our model demonstrates the ability to generate novel crystalline porous materials that are not present in the training dataset, while exhibiting exceptional performance in inverse design tasks targeted on various chemical properties including the void fraction, Henry coefficient and heat of adsorption. Comparing our model with a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) revealed that the diffusion model outperforms the GAN in terms of structure validity, exhibiting an over 2000-fold improvement in performance. We firmly believe that diffusion models (along with other deep generative models) hold immense potential in revolutionizing the design of new materials, and anticipate the wide extension of our model to other classes of porous materials.

methods.value: The authors developed a new diffusion model named zeolite diffusion (ZeoDiﬀ) based on the Denoising Diﬀusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) framework, using three-dimensional grids composed of energy, silicon, and oxygen channels as input representation.

problems.value: The generation of porous materials using diffusion models remains unexplored due to challenges arising from the relatively large number of atoms and the difficulty in capturing essential topological features.

hypotheses.value: A diffusion model can be developed to generate pure silica zeolites, marking one of the first applications of diffusion models to porous materials.

evidence.value: The model successfully generated structures with high validity while exhibiting exceptional capabilities in inverse design at the same time. Quantitative comparisons with GAN demonstrated that the diffusion model outperforms GAN by more than 2000 times in terms of structure validity.

conclusions.value: The diffusion model developed in this work can generate new zeolite structures unseen during the training phase and demonstrates vast improvement over the GAN model under the same conditions.
